title: STEM Quick Starts: Angles & Lines, Sig Figs & Unit Conversions
details:
A set of short, high-impact flashcard modules for Grades 7–11.
Front = task/question. Back = rule/answer + the most common trap.
No tests, no tags—pure practice for fast confidence.

modules.moduleDescription: Angle types + the two fastest sums in geometry (90° and 180°). Build instant recognition and 1-step solving.

cards.title: What is an acute/right/obtuse/straight/reflex angle?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute <90°, Right=90°, Obtuse 90–180°, Straight=180°, Reflex >180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What does complementary mean?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Complementary angles sum to 90° (often split right angles).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What does supplementary mean?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Supplementary angles sum to 180° (often linear pairs/straight lines).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What does perpendicular mean (in degrees)?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Perpendicular lines form 90° angles.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is a straight angle?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A straight angle is exactly 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you use angle addition?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Whole angle = sum of its parts (angle addition).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: When do angles add to 90°?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Complementary angles sum to 90° (often split right angles).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: When do angles add to 180°?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Supplementary angles sum to 180° (often linear pairs/straight lines).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How can you quickly tell obtuse vs reflex?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute <90°, Right=90°, Obtuse 90–180°, Straight=180°, Reflex >180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What’s the fastest way to solve x in split right angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Complementary angles sum to 90° (often split right angles).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What’s the fastest way to solve x in a straight line?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Supplementary angles sum to 180° (often linear pairs/straight lines).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What must be true to call an angle 'right'?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute <90°, Right=90°, Obtuse 90–180°, Straight=180°, Reflex >180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is the rule for a right angle split into two angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Complementary angles sum to 90° (often split right angles).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How can you check if an angle is reflex?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute <90°, Right=90°, Obtuse 90–180°, Straight=180°, Reflex >180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is angle addition in one line?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Whole angle = sum of its parts (angle addition).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is the relationship between a straight line and 180°?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A straight angle is exactly 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you recognize complementary in a diagram?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Complementary angles sum to 90° (often split right angles).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you recognize supplementary in a diagram?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Supplementary angles sum to 180° (often linear pairs/straight lines).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What’s the degree measure of a right angle?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acute <90°, Right=90°, Obtuse 90–180°, Straight=180°, Reflex >180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you verify your angle answer quickly?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Whole angle = sum of its parts (angle addition).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: Classify 35°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Acute.
Trap: Don’t confuse with complementary; classification is about size only.

cards.title: Classify 90°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Right.
Trap: 90° is exactly right—no rounding.

cards.title: Classify 179°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Obtuse.
Trap: Reflex is >180°, not 'close to 180'.

cards.title: Classify 181°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Reflex.
Trap: Anything >180° is reflex even if barely.

cards.title: An angle is 38°. Find its complement.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 52°.
Trap: Complement means sum to 90°, not 180°.

cards.title: An angle is 112°. Find its supplement.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 68°.
Trap: Supplement means sum to 180°.

cards.title: Two angles are complementary. One is 27°. Find the other.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 63°.
Trap: Don’t subtract from 180°.

cards.title: Two angles are supplementary. One is 141°. Find the other.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 39°.
Trap: Don’t subtract from 90°.

cards.title: A right angle is split into 35° and x. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 55°.
Trap: Right angle total is 90°.

cards.title: A straight angle is split into 125° and x. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 55°.
Trap: Straight line total is 180°.

cards.title: Angle ABC is split into 25° and (2x)°. Total is 85°. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30°.
Trap: Use angle addition: 25+2x=85.

cards.title: An angle is split into (x)° and (x+18)°. Total is 90°. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 36°.
Trap: Total 90° implies complementary.

cards.title: An angle is split into (3x)° and 24°. Total is 180°. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 52°.
Trap: 3x+24=180.

cards.title: If two lines are perpendicular, what is the measure of each angle at the intersection?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 90°.
Trap: Perpendicular does not mean 'equal' in other contexts—here it forces 90°.

cards.title: Find the missing angle: 90° total, one part is 49°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 41°.
Trap: Subtract from 90°.

cards.title: Find the missing angle: 180° total, one part is 73°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 107°.
Trap: Subtract from 180°.

cards.title: Angle is 0.5 of a straight angle. Find the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 90°.
Trap: Half of 180° is 90°.

cards.title: Angle is 0.25 of a right angle. Find the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 22.5°.
Trap: Right angle is 90° → quarter is 22.5.

cards.title: Classify 270°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Reflex.
Trap: 270° is not straight; straight is 180°.

cards.title: A reflex angle is 240°. Find the smaller angle that completes a full turn.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 120°.
Trap: Full turn is 360°; 360−240.

cards.title: A complement is 17° more than the angle. Find the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 36.5°.
Trap: Let x+(x+17)=90.

cards.title: A supplement is 5° less than the angle. Find the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 92.5°.
Trap: Let x+(x−5)=180.

cards.title: Angle is split into 3 equal parts and totals 90°. Find one part.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30°.
Trap: 90/3.

cards.title: Angle is split into 4 equal parts and totals 180°. Find one part.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 45°.
Trap: 180/4.

cards.title: Is 95° complementary to 5°?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: No; they sum to 100°.
Trap: Complementary must sum to 90° exactly.

cards.title: Is 110° supplementary to 70°?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Yes; 110+70=180°.
Trap: Check the sum.

cards.title: One angle is 2x and its complement is x+15. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 25°.
Trap: 2x+(x+15)=90.

cards.title: One angle is 4x and its supplement is 2x+30. Find x.
A straight angle is split into angles in ratio 2:3. Find the larger angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 108°.
Trap: 2k+3k=180 → k=36.

cards.title: A right angle is split into angles in ratio 1:2. Find the smaller angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30°.
Trap: k+2k=90 → k=30.

cards.title: Classify 89.9°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Acute.
Trap: Acute is <90° (even if very close).

cards.title: Classify 90.1°.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Obtuse.
Trap: Obtuse starts just above 90°.

cards.title: A supplement is twice the angle. Find the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 60°.
Trap: x+2x=180.

cards.title: A complement is three times the angle. Find the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 22.5°.
Trap: x+3x=90.

cards.title: Two complementary angles differ by 12°. Find the larger.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 51°.
Trap: x+(x−12)=90.

cards.title: Two supplementary angles differ by 40°. Find the smaller.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 70°.
Trap: x+(x+40)=180.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Complementary angles add to 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Complementary add to 90°.
Quick check: Ask: is it 90 or 180?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Supplementary angles add to 90°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Supplementary add to 180°.
Quick check: Ask: straight line?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 179° is reflex.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Reflex is >180°. 179° is obtuse.
Quick check: Check: is it greater than 180?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 180° is obtuse.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 180° is straight.
Quick check: Memorize: straight = 180.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 90° is acute.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 90° is right.
Quick check: Acute must be less than 90.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Perpendicular lines form 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Perpendicular means 90°.
Quick check: Perpendicular → right angle.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If angles share a vertex, they’re complementary.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Sharing a vertex isn’t enough; check the total.
Quick check: Always check the sum.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: A reflex angle is between 90° and 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: That’s obtuse; reflex is >180°.
Quick check: Reflex exceeds a straight angle.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: To find a complement, subtract from 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Subtract from 90°.
Quick check: Complement → 90.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: To find a supplement, subtract from 90°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Subtract from 180°.
Quick check: Supplement → 180.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Angle addition means multiply angles.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Angle addition means add parts to get the whole.
Quick check: Whole = part + part.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 360° is a straight line.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Straight is 180°; 360° is a full turn.
Quick check: Know 90/180/360.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 90° is supplementary to 90°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Yes, 90+90=180, but that’s supplementary—not complementary.
Quick check: Check which sum you’re asked for.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 45° and 45° are supplementary.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: They’re complementary (sum 90°).
Quick check: 45+45=90.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If total is 180°, use complementary.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Total 180° is supplementary.
Quick check: Match the total.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If total is 90°, use supplementary.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Total 90° is complementary.
Quick check: Match the total.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: An obtuse angle can be 200°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 200° is reflex.
Quick check: Obtuse is <180.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Any two angles that add to 180° must be a linear pair.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: They could be separate; linear pair requires a straight line.
Quick check: Ask: do they form a straight line?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 0° is acute.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Acute is >0 and <90; 0° is neither (degenerate).
Quick check: Acute means strictly between.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: A complement is always smaller than the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Not always (e.g., 10° has complement 80°).
Quick check: Compare after computing.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: A supplement is always bigger than the angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Not always (e.g., 100° has supplement 80°).
Quick check: Compute before judging.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If an angle is split equally, you still subtract.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Use division when parts are equal.
Quick check: Equal parts → divide total.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 89.9° rounds to right angle in geometry.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Classification uses exact definition; 89.9° is acute.
Quick check: Don’t round classifications.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 180° has a complement of 0°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Complement applies to angles that sum to 90; 180° can’t have a complement.
Quick check: Complement only for totals of 90.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Complementary/supplementary depends on position, not sum.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It depends on the sum (90 or 180).
Quick check: Always check the total.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: A straight angle plus a right angle is 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 180+90=270.
Quick check: Add correctly before labeling.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If one part is 125° in a straight angle, the other is 65°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It’s 55° (180−125).
Quick check: Subtract carefully.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 180−73=97.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It’s 107.
Quick check: Do the subtraction carefully.

modules.title: Complementary vs Supplementary Angles (90° & 180°)

modules.moduleDescription: Intersection patterns: vertical angles, linear pairs, adjacent vs vertical, and quick x-equations.

cards.title: What are vertical angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is a linear pair?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: Are adjacent angles always equal?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Adjacent angles share a side; they are NOT automatically equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: When do you use 360° around a point?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Angles around a point sum to 360° (use only when all angles around vertex are included).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you solve x using vertical angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you solve x using a linear pair?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What’s the difference between adjacent and vertical angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Adjacent angles share a side; they are NOT automatically equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What must be true for angles to be a linear pair?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What’s a fast check after solving an intersection problem?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is the 'opposite angles' rule?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: When should you NOT use 360°?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Angles around a point sum to 360° (use only when all angles around vertex are included).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you identify the straight line in a drawing?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What relationship is always equal at an intersection?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What relationship always sums to 180° at an intersection?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you decide between 'equal' and 'sum 180'?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is 'angles around a point' in one line?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Angles around a point sum to 360° (use only when all angles around vertex are included).
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What does 'adjacent' mean in geometry?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Adjacent angles share a side; they are NOT automatically equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What is the quickest way to label intersection angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Vertical (opposite) angles are equal.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: What’s the most common intersection trap?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: How do you check your algebra in angle equations?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A linear pair forms a straight line → sum is 180°.
Quick check: Say what must be true for this rule to apply.

cards.title: Two lines intersect. One angle is 35°. Find its vertical angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 35°.
Trap: Vertical angles are equal; don’t use 180° here.

cards.title: Two lines intersect. One angle is 128°. Find an adjacent linear‑pair angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 52°.
Trap: Adjacent is not always 180—only a linear pair is.

cards.title: At an intersection, angle A is 70°. What is the angle adjacent to A on a straight line?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 110°.
Trap: Linear pair sums to 180.

cards.title: If one angle is 95°, what are the measures of the other three intersection angles?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 95°, 85°, 95°.
Trap: Vertical equal; adjacent supplementary.

cards.title: Vertical angles are x and 3x−20. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 10.
Trap: Set equal: x=3x−20.

cards.title: Linear pair angles are x and 2x+30. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 50.
Trap: x+(2x+30)=180.

cards.title: One angle is 4x+10. Its vertical is 2x+70. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30.
Trap: Vertical angles equal.

cards.title: One angle is 5x−15. Its linear pair is 2x+45. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 50.
Trap: Sum to 180.

cards.title: An intersection angle is 60°. What is the angle next to it (forming a straight line)?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 120°.
Trap: Adjacent isn’t enough—must be straight line.

cards.title: Angles around a point are 110°, 70°, and x. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 180°.
Trap: Use 360° only when you have all angles around the point.

cards.title: Angles around a point are x, x, and 120°. Find x.
At an intersection, two adjacent angles are (x+20) and (3x−10) and form a linear pair. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 42.5.
Trap: Add to 180; don’t set equal.

cards.title: At an intersection, two angles are labeled as vertical: (2x+15) and (5x−45). Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 20.
Trap: Set equal.

cards.title: One angle is 140°. What is the vertical angle? What is the linear-pair angle?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 140° and 40°.
Trap: Different relationships.

cards.title: If two vertical angles are each (x+5)° and one adjacent is 3x°, find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 10.
Trap: Adjacent to (x+5) forms 180.

cards.title: Angles around a point: 90°, 90°, 45°, and x. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 135°.
Trap: Sum to 360.

cards.title: At an intersection, angle A is 75°. What is the angle opposite A?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 75°.
Trap: Opposite (vertical) is equal.

cards.title: At an intersection, one angle is x and an adjacent linear-pair angle is x+40. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 70.
Trap: x+(x+40)=180.

cards.title: If vertical angles are 2x and 7x−50, find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 10.
Trap: 2x=7x−50.

cards.title: If a linear pair is 3x and x+60, find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30.
Trap: 3x+(x+60)=180.

cards.title: At an intersection, one angle is 15° more than its vertical. Is that possible?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: No.
Trap: Vertical angles must be equal.

cards.title: Angles around a point: 100°, 100°, 80°, and x. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 80°.
Trap: Sum to 360.

cards.title: At an intersection, an angle is 89°. What is its linear-pair angle?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 91°.
Trap: 180−89.

cards.title: At an intersection, an angle is 101°. What is its vertical angle?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 101°.
Trap: Equal.

cards.title: If one angle is 30°, are the two adjacent angles equal?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Yes (150° and 150°).
Trap: Adjacent can be equal here, but not always.

cards.title: Angles around a point: x, 2x, 3x, 60. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 50°.
Trap: x+2x+3x+60=360.

cards.title: An angle is 44°. Find its vertical and linear-pair angles.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 44° and 136°.
Trap: Keep them distinct.

cards.title: At an intersection, an angle is (x−12). Its linear pair is (2x+6). Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 62.
Trap: Sum 180.

cards.title: At an intersection, an angle is (3x). Its vertical is (x+50). Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 25.
Trap: Set equal.

cards.title: Angles around a point: 135°, 90°, x, x. Find x.
At an intersection, one angle is 180°−x and its vertical is 120°. Find x.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 60.
Trap: Vertical: 180−x=120.

cards.title: At an intersection, one angle is 90°. What can you say about the lines?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: They are perpendicular.
Trap: A right angle at intersection implies perpendicular.

cards.title: At an intersection, an angle is 0°. What does that mean?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: Lines overlap (degenerate).
Trap: Not a typical intersection problem.

cards.title: If one angle is 170°, find the smallest intersection angle.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 10°.
Trap: Linear pair gives 10.

cards.title: Linear pair angles are equal. What are they?
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 90° and 90°.
Trap: x+x=180.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Adjacent angles are always equal.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Adjacent only means sharing a side; equality is not guaranteed.
Quick check: Ask: which relationship is given?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Vertical angles add to 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Vertical angles are equal; linear pairs add to 180°.
Quick check: Equal vs sum.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If two angles share a vertex, they’re vertical.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Vertical angles are opposite; sharing a vertex isn’t enough.
Quick check: Opposite across intersection?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Use 360° for every intersection problem.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Use 360° only when summing all angles around the point.
Quick check: Do you have all angles?

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Linear pair angles are opposite.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Opposite are vertical; linear pair are adjacent on a straight line.
Quick check: Opposite vs adjacent.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If one angle is 128°, its vertical is 52°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Vertical is 128°; 52° is the linear pair.
Quick check: Opposite = equal.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If angles are labeled vertical, set them to 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Vertical → set equal; linear pair → sum to 180.
Quick check: Match the rule.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Around-a-point sum is 180°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Around a point sums to 360°.
Quick check: Full turn check.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If two adjacent angles add to 180°, they must be vertical.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Adding to 180 makes them supplementary/linear pair, not vertical.
Quick check: Vertical means equal.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 180−89=99.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 180−89=91.
Quick check: Re-check subtraction.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If one angle is 101°, all angles are 101°.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Only the vertical is 101°; adjacent are 79°.
Quick check: Use both rules.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: A right angle at an intersection doesn’t tell you anything.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It tells you the lines are perpendicular.
Quick check: Right angle → perpendicular.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: If vertical angles are x and 3x, x can be any value.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Vertical angles must be equal → x=0 (degenerate) if x=3x.
Quick check: Set equal first.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Linear pair means the angles are equal.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Linear pair means sum is 180°.
Quick check: Sum, not equal.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: In x+(x+40)=180, x=110.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Correct is x=70.
Quick check: Solve carefully.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: You can pick any two angles and call them a linear pair.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: They must be adjacent and form a straight line.
Quick check: Look for straight line.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 2x=7x−50 gives x=−10.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Correct is x=10.
Quick check: Add/subtract correctly.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Vertical angles share a side.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Adjacent share a side; vertical do not.
Quick check: Side-sharing check.

Answer: 120 mA.
Trap: milli = ×1000.

cards.title: Convert 5.0×10^6 μs to s.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 5.0 s.
Trap: μ = 10^-6 so 10^6 μs = 1 s.

cards.title: Convert 72 in to ft.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 6 ft.
Trap: 12 in = 1 ft.

cards.title: Convert 1.0 ft² to in².
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 144 in².
Trap: Square the 12: 12²=144.

cards.title: Convert 2.0 mi to km (1 mi = 1.609 km).
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 3.22 km.
Trap: Use given factor; keep units consistent.

cards.title: Convert 55 mph to m/s (1 mi=1609 m, 1 h=3600 s).
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 24.6 m/s.
Trap: Convert miles→meters and hours→seconds.

cards.title: Convert 3.5×10^2 nm to μm.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 0.35 μm.
Trap: 1 μm = 1000 nm.

cards.title: Convert 0.0030 m² to cm².
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30 cm².
Trap: 0.0030×10,000.

cards.title: Convert 2.0×10^-3 L to mL.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 2.0 mL.
Trap: ×1000.

cards.title: Convert 8.0×10^4 mg to kg.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 0.080 kg.
Trap: mg→g→kg (10^6 mg = 1 kg).

cards.title: Convert 0.50 mm to μm.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 500 μm.
Trap: 1 mm = 1000 μm.

cards.title: Convert 250 ns to s.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 2.50×10^-7 s.
Trap: nano = 10^-9.

cards.title: Convert 3.0×10^-2 kg to g.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 30 g.
Trap: ×1000.

cards.title: Convert 9.0 cm to m.
cards.cardDescription:
Answer: 0.090 m.
Trap: Divide by 100; keep zeros meaningful if needed.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 3.6 km = 0.0036 m.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: You multiply by 1000: 3.6 km = 3600 m.
Quick check: kilo means bigger.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 75 cm = 75 m.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: centi means 1/100: 75 cm = 0.75 m.
Quick check: Check prefix power.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: In factor‑label, you add units.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: You multiply by a fraction equal to 1 so units cancel.
Quick check: Write units on every step.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 2.0 m² = 200 cm².
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It’s 20,000 cm² because you square the 100.
Quick check: Square the conversion.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 3.0 m³ = 300 cm³.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It’s 3,000,000 cm³ because you cube the 100.
Quick check: Cube the conversion.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: μ means milli.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: μ is micro (10^-6); milli is m (10^-3).
Quick check: Symbol check.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: m means meter everywhere.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: m can be meter or milli‑ prefix; context matters.
Quick check: Prefix vs unit symbol.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: k means kelvin.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: k is kilo; K is kelvin.
Quick check: Case matters.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 90 km/h to m/s: divide by 3.6.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: You divide by 3.6 to go km/h→m/s (so 90/3.6=25).
Quick check: Remember 3.6 factor.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 12 m/s to km/h: divide by 3.6.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: You multiply by 3.6 (12×3.6=43.2).
Quick check: Direction check.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 1 L = 100 cm³.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 1 L = 1000 cm³.
Quick check: Know the key equivalence.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 1000 μm = 1 m.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 1000 μm = 1 mm.
Quick check: Micro to milli step.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: Cancel units across addition/subtraction.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: You can cancel units only in multiplication/division.
Quick check: Units must match to add/subtract.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: You can cancel units before writing the conversion factor.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Write the full factor first; then cancel.
Quick check: Write → then cancel.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 0.0045 m to mm: divide by 1000.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Multiply by 1000 → 4.5 mm.
Quick check: m→mm gets bigger.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 6500 μm to mm: multiply by 1000.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Divide by 1000 → 6.5 mm.
Quick check: μm→mm gets smaller.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 1 ft² = 12 in².
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It’s 144 in² (12²).
Quick check: Square the conversion.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: nano is 10^-6.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: nano is 10^-9.
Quick check: Prefix power check.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 250 ns = 2.50×10^-9 s.
Spot the mistake: Derived units don’t matter; only numbers do.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Units confirm formulas and catch mistakes.
Quick check: Unit sanity check.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: mph to m/s: only convert miles to meters.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: You must also convert hours to seconds.
Quick check: Convert both distance and time.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 8.0×10^4 mg = 0.80 kg.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: It’s 0.080 kg (10^6 mg = 1 kg).
Quick check: Powers of 10.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 101.3 kPa = 101.3 Pa.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: kPa to Pa multiply by 1000 → 101,300 Pa.
Quick check: kilo = 10^3.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: You can flip a conversion factor anytime.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Flip only if it still equals 1 and cancels the right unit.
Quick check: Cancellation goal.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 9000 μs = 9 s.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 9000 μs = 0.009 s.
Quick check: Micro is 10^-6.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 2.0 mi = 2.0×1.609 km = 3.218 km → 3.2180 km.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Round based on sig figs: 2.0 has 2 sig figs → 3.2 km.
Quick check: Sig figs apply if needed.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: In density g/mL to kg/L, you must multiply by 1000.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: 1 g/mL equals 1 kg/L directly.
Quick check: Key equivalence.

cards.title: Spot the mistake: 0.0030 m² to cm²: multiply by 100.
cards.cardDescription:
Fix: Multiply by 10,000 (100²).
Quick check: Area uses squared factor.
